sources.title: "Siren of the Resistance: The Artistry and Espionage of Josephine Baker" (The National WWII Museum)
Cardiff University historian's research on Baker's WWII espionage contribution
National Women's History Museum biography of Josephine Baker
"Dancer, singer, activist, spy: the extraordinary life of Josephine Baker" (FRANCE 24) -- documents the 1964-1969 financial collapse and 1973 comeback

risk_tolerance.rationale: Two independent, extreme, well-documented high-stakes instances: became an active wartime intelligence agent for the French Resistance after the fall of Paris, physically smuggling intelligence in invisible ink on her own sheet music and hidden on her body, deliberately relying on her fame to avoid thorough searches -- a role carrying real mortal danger under Nazi occupation; and, separately, sailed to Paris at 19 with no guarantee of success to pursue a stage career.

persistence.rationale: Two independent, extreme, well-documented instances of rebuilding from total loss: ran away from an extremely poor and dangerous childhood at 13 and built a sustained, escalating performance career from nothing; and, after total financial and material collapse -- her estate auctioned off and she had to be forced from the building after barricading herself inside in 1969 -- staged a full professional comeback at age 67, culminating in four sold-out performances at Carnegie Hall.

impact_motivation.rationale: Adopted twelve children of different ethnic, national, and religious backgrounds specifically and deliberately to publicly demonstrate that racial and cultural harmony was possible, calling them her "Rainbow Tribe" and touring publicly with them -- a sustained, real, long-term family-building and advocacy commitment, not a symbolic gesture.

autonomy_need.rationale: Quit school and left home at 12-13, living on the streets and scavenging for food rather than remaining in her circumstances, a single but extreme, early documented act of self-directed departure from her family situation.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained a public refusal to perform for segregated audiences throughout her career at real professional and economic cost, and was the only woman to speak at the 1963 March on Washington, taking the microphone directly after Martin Luther King's "I Have a Dream" speech.

proactive_agency.rationale: Her wartime espionage role was accepted well beyond any obligation her celebrity status carried, and her sustained civil-rights activism (refusing segregated venues, the March on Washington appearance) was similarly self-directed beyond her professional entertainment career, not required by any external role.

resourcefulness.rationale: Devised a specific, creative operational method for wartime intelligence smuggling -- writing in invisible ink on her own sheet music and pinning notes inside her underwear -- deliberately exploiting her celebrity status as cover, a single but very concrete, ingenious documented instance.

provenance.notes: Roster-1000 session 15 (tightly controlled 4-person calibration experiment, docs/roster-1000-checkpoint.md Sec.81): selected specifically for domain breadth (entertainment/activism/exploration) AND for an unusually well-documented public life spanning multiple distinct careers. 5 substantive sources consulted (Wikipedia for orientation only, plus 4 independent sources: the National WWII Museum's espionage account, a Cardiff University historian's dedicated research on her wartime contribution, the National Women's History Museum's biography, and a FRANCE 24 account of her financial collapse and comeback). Evidence ledger: 16 distinct, source-attributed episodes, spanning at least 6 life periods (St Louis childhood, early stage career, 1925 Paris stardom, WWII espionage, the civil-rights era, later-life financial collapse and comeback) and at least 6 behavioral contexts (solitary survival, career risk-taking, wartime risk/resourcefulness, principled public conflict, family-building/advocacy, persistence through total loss). Ledger built and locked BEFORE any trait score was assigned; trait scores locked BEFORE eligibility_v2 was consulted.
